name: Juicy wash and go
tagline: Conditioned, clumped and fully dried, so the definition is still there on day three.
image_alt: A rounded wash-and-go with defined coils and the front curls left to fall forward.
description: A botanical-forward wash and go built around a hooded-dryer set: what juicy actually means, the ten-step ritual, how to pick one botanical gel, and how to keep the style for a week.
intro: A juicy wash and go is not a wet one. It is conditioned, well clumped, set under a hooded dryer until completely dry, then released gently. This plan uses botanical-forward gels and no air-drying.

causes.title: What juicy actually means
causes.intro: Four words get used as if they mean the same thing. They overlap, but they are not identical.
items: Hair that is well conditioned and flexible.
This is the foundation. No gel can make up for tangled, under-conditioned hair.
The look of defined, well-conditioned coils that catch the light.
It comes from clumping and conditioning, not from being wet.
A styling finish, while the hair is still wet.
It looks great for twenty minutes. It is not the goal.
A properly set wash and go
A style that has dried completely, formed its shape and held it.
This is the goal. The set is the part people rush.
Plant gels such as flax, okra, aloe and marshmallow give slip while you style, help strands group into clumps, and leave a dried film that keeps the shape. That film is a scaffold for the style.
It does not seal water inside the strand, and it does not stop breakage. The honest promise is a more manageable style with less daily handling.

stock.title: Are you ready to style?
stock.intro: You do not need perfect hair first. You need manageable hair. If most of these are a yes, go straight to the ritual. If not, the optional prep below is for you.
items: Your hair is reasonably easy to detangle with conditioner in it.
Ends are not rough or knotted
Check the last few inches first.
No film, no waxy feel, no heaviness from old product.
No itch, tightness or flaking you are trying to style over.

routine.title: The ritual
routine.intro: One complete wash, style and hooded-dryer set. Give it a free afternoon the first time.

wash.title: Wash, style and set
steps: Saturate
Wet your hair in four to eight sections and make sure the roots and the inside of each section are soaked. Dense hair can be dripping outside and dry in the middle.
Shampoo
Shampoo the scalp, let the lather rinse down the lengths, and rinse well. There is no need to scrub the ends. Clarify or chelate only when your hair needs it.
Deep condition
Apply a moisture-rich mask to each section and leave it on for as long as its label says. Warmth is fine if the label allows it.
Detangle
Fingers first, then a wide-tooth comb or detangling brush, ends toward roots, with enough conditioner for real slip. Remove the shed hair now, before any gel goes on.
Rinse and check
Hair should feel soft, slippery and flexible, not waxy. This is the moment to decide whether you need a leave-in at all.
Add a leave-in, if needed
A light layer on soaking wet hair, just enough for slip. If your gel already gives you slip, skip it. Test any new leave-in and gel pairing on one small section first.
Apply the botanical gel
Hair must be very wet, not damp. Work in small sections with praying hands and smooth from roots to ends. Shingle only the sections that need more definition, then leave each one alone.
Shape and elongate
Encourage natural clumps and smooth each section with gentle tension. No hard pulling and no tight root stretching.
Set under the hooded dryer
Arrange the coils in their final shape, then dry at a comfortable temperature until completely dry, roots and inside included. Let the hair cool before you touch it.
Release and polish
When it is fully dry and cool, rub a drop or two of lightweight oil between your palms, scrunch the lengths gently, and break the cast without pulling every clump apart.

between.title: The first week
groups: Break the cast once it is fully dry. Arrange the roots. Protect it at night.
Wear it loose or in a loose pineapple. Satin bonnet at night. Do not add gel just because the hair has moved.
Mist lightly, put a tiny amount of leave-in on frizzy spots, smooth those sections, add a little compatible gel only where needed, and dry them completely.
Keep the ends protected at night and avoid tight styles. Wash sooner if your scalp needs it or the style gets coated or tangled.

techniques.title: The rules of this plan
techniques.intro: These are the choices that make this a juicy wash and go and not just a wash and go.
items: The hooded dryer is the whole point. It gives a complete, predictable set with the least handling of wet hair. Do not shortcut it by air-drying or by sleeping on damp hair.
Drying time depends on density, length, how much product you used and your dryer, so go by how the hair feels, not by a number of minutes.
Choose your hold from plant gels. No synthetic gel toppers, and no polymer-heavy hold products.
A botanical extract on the label does not mean a formula is free of synthetic polymers. Read the complete ingredient list.
Build coherent groups of coils and leave them alone.
Every extra rake, separation or fluff before the set is dry breaks definition you have just made.
Do not break the cast early
The cast is the dried gel film. A firm cast is not a problem. It is what makes the style last.
Judge softness after it is dry and released, not while the gel is still setting.
Use less product than you think
One gel to start. A second only if you need more hold.
It is much easier to find what works, and avoid buildup, when only one thing changes at a time.
Satin bonnet or pillowcase, ends tucked in, nothing tight.
Your night routine decides how much of the definition survives.

rota.title: Optional prep
rota.intro: If your hair is dry, tangled, breaking or coated, take two to four weeks to get it ready before the full ritual. If it is already soft and manageable, skip this and go straight to the ritual.
phases: Remove buildup, set a conditioned baseline, and check strength. One focus per wash day.
items: Shampoo, clarify if there is buildup, chelate if your water is hard, deep condition, detangle, light leave-in, loose protective style.
A conditioner with ceramides and other supportive lipids. Then your normal leave-in and a protective style.
Only if your hair has been bleached, relaxed, heavily heat-styled or is breaking. Otherwise deep condition as normal.
Moisture deep conditioner, gentle detangling, leave-in, low-manipulation style. Aim for flexible and manageable, not as soft as possible.
rota.note: If your hair is badly damaged or chemically processed, a stylist may be a better first step than any calendar.

use.title: What to use
use.intro: Products by the job they do in this plan. Our catalog is still growing, so some rows are empty for now.
items: Cleanses the scalp without leaving the lengths hard to detangle.
The foundation. Botanical slip plus conditioning agents.
Lipid-supporting conditioning. It does not replace your deep conditioner.
A light layer for slip. Skip it if your gel already has enough.
Your main product. Pick one from the shortlist below.
A drop or two of lightweight jojoba or squalane on fully dry hair. The aim is soft definition, not an oil slick.

choose.title: Pick one gel
choose.intro: Test one botanical gel on its own before you try anything else. You do not need four gels for a beautiful wash and go.
items: Use one gel for the first wash day. Add a second only if you need more hold, and test the pair on one section first.
Water first, then plant extracts and pectin or gums, is what you are looking for. Synthetic polymers or thickeners further down the list mean it is botanical-forward, not botanical-only.
Some botanical gels also contain hydrolysed protein. If you are tracking protein, check for it.

shortlist.title: Botanical gels to try
items: Botanical base gel. Slip and definition
Firmer cast. Its list includes carbomer, so botanical-forward rather than botanical-only

ing.title: What to look for on a label
ing.intro: The plant ingredients that do the styling work. Hover any name to see what it is.
items: Mucilage that gives slip while you style and forms a film as it dries. Flexible to firm, depending on the formula.
Slippery plant extracts for glide while you detangle and apply.
Water-loving ingredients that add a light, flexible base.
Plant gums that thicken the gel and form the film that holds the clump.
Jojoba, squalane, cetearyl alcohol. Softness and less friction. Keep oil for the finish.

trouble.title: If something feels off
items: A strong cast or too much gel. Wait until it is completely dry before scrunching, and use less next time.
Two products that do not layer well, or too many layers. Simplify and test pairs on one section.
Not enough conditioning, or buildup. Look at your deep conditioner and your cleansing before adding product.
It has not finished drying, or the formula is very humectant-heavy. Keep drying, then adjust.
Poor clumping or too little hold. Smaller sections, even distribution, hands off.
Friction, humidity or weak hold. Improve the set and your night protection.
Detangle the nape well before styling and protect it overnight.
Too much product near the scalp. Use less at the roots.

end.title: After your first set
notes: Judge the wash and go once it is dry and released, not while it is wet. That is the only version that tells you whether it worked.

A homemade gel is a different thing: water-based recipes grow bacteria unless they are properly preserved, and refrigerating or adding vitamin E does not fix that. If you make your own, make a tiny batch, use clean tools, keep it cold and throw it out quickly.
list: Hair was fully saturated before styling
Hair felt soft and flexible after conditioning
Gel was spread evenly, roots to ends
Roots and inside were completely dry
Cast was released only when fully dry
Curls feel soft and still hold their shape
